results.label: thm:main
results.title: Sharp uniform late coefficients
results.claim_summary: The conjectured hyperbolic late-coefficient amplitudes have an explicit first inverse-index correction, uniformly on every fixed complex disk |u|≤U; the odd normalized error has an extra factor |u|.
scope_limits: The quotient at u=0 is removable; all constants may depend on the fixed U.
Relative versions are uniform for real 0<u≤U. At complex zeros of a parity amplitude, the additive expansion is the available statement.
No estimate for growing |u|, ordinary summation, or an optimally truncated physical remainder is claimed.
results.attribution_note: Proves and strengthens the explicitly conjectural amplitudes in predecessor §11.1. No worldwide priority claim for the general endpoint mechanism.

results.label: thm:analytic-preview
results.title: Borel radius and continuation
results.claim_summary: For fixed complex u≠0, the shifted Borel transform has exact radius A and genuine singularities at both ±A, continues along paths avoiding Aℤ after the starting origin, and the formal inverse V is 1-summable in every nonreal direction.
scope_limits: At u=0 the transform and formal inverse vanish identically.
Aℤ is an allowed obstruction set, not a claim that every point is active on every sheet.
The preview is not used as an independent proof input.
results.attribution_note: Summary of separately proved coefficient and analytic results.

results.label: prop:lagrange
results.title: Exact finite reversion

article_section.label: sec:forward
article_section.title: The forward expansion and the exact reversion formula

results.claim_summary: There is a unique zero-constant formal solution V∈qQ[u][[q]], and each coefficient is given by a finite Lagrange sum with an explicit polynomial T_{n,k}.
scope_limits: Exact for every integer n≥1, with q and u independent formal variables.
The formula does not require or imply convergence of the formal forward tail.
results.attribution_note: Already proved in the predecessor; rederived by auxiliary-variable formal Lagrange inversion.

results.label: prop:structure
results.title: Signs, valuations, and the first coefficients

article_section.label: sec:forward
article_section.title: The forward expansion and the exact reversion formula

results.claim_summary: Every C_n has alternating coefficientwise sign, exact degree 2n−1, the displayed Catalan top coefficient, and exact valuation one for n=1 or even n and two for odd n≥3.
scope_limits: These sign and valuation statements use the specific Lambert forward support; they are not automatically preserved by arbitrary polynomial perturbations.
results.attribution_note: Inherited structural statements with a direct local proof.

results.label: lem:factorial
results.title: Endpoint-preserving factorial bounds

article_section.label: sec:leading
article_section.title: Uniform factorial convolution and the hyperbolic amplitudes

results.claim_summary: Elementary factorial convolution bounds retain the large endpoint and give a summable-in-k majorant for the complete finite Lagrange sum.
scope_limits: For the Lambert coefficients choose K≥max(c,4ζ(2)²); S_{n,k} uses the nonnegative scaled coefficients a_m.
The bounds cover k=n; they are estimates, not sharp constants for every convolution.
results.attribution_note: Proved elementary estimate supplying the uniform step in the project conjecture. The factorial endpoint mechanism has established antecedents.

results.label: lem:endpoint
results.title: First endpoint extraction

article_section.label: sec:leading
article_section.title: Uniform factorial convolution and the hyperbolic amplitudes

results.claim_summary: Extracts configurations with one index greater than one and bounds all remaining compositions by a marked-pair interior convolution.
scope_limits: The displayed range is k≥2 and n≥k+2; k=1 is exact.
Nonnegativity is for the scaled Lambert input. The finite-phase theorem uses the corresponding absolute-value bound.
results.attribution_note: Direct quantitative endpoint extraction used in the uniform proof.

results.label: thm:leading-rate
results.title: A quantified proof of the source conjecture

article_section.label: sec:leading
article_section.title: Uniform factorial convolution and the hyperbolic amplitudes

results.claim_summary: Proves the predecessor’s two hyperbolic amplitude conjectures with quantified, locally complex-uniform O(1/n) errors after the correct parity-dependent valuation is removed.
scope_limits: Uniform for |u|≤U with removable quotients at u=0.
The real relative equivalents hold uniformly for 0<u≤U; no lower bound on u is required.
The large-k tail estimate is essential; fixed-k limits alone do not justify this result.
results.attribution_note: New proof of a specific stated project conjecture, with stronger parameter uniformity.

results.label: cor:moving-u
results.title: Two limits may be taken together

article_section.label: sec:leading
article_section.title: Uniform factorial convolution and the hyperbolic amplitudes

results.claim_summary: The coefficient index and a positive slow parameter tending to zero may approach their limits together at any rate.
scope_limits: Assumes u_n>0, u_n→0, and n→∞ through the indicated parity.
No coupling-rate restriction is imposed. This is not a theorem about ordinary sector summation or physical optimal truncation.
results.attribution_note: Uniform consequence of the resolved amplitude conjecture.

results.label: thm:finite-phases
results.title: Leading amplitudes for finitely many phases

article_section.label: sec:phases
article_section.title: Finite phases and changes of the initial coefficients

results.claim_summary: For an arbitrary formal input with finitely many equal-modulus factorial phases, the nonlinear inverse multiplies each leading phase amplitude by exp(Aρu/ω), where ρ is the linear forward coefficient.
formula_latex: |\widetilde r_n|\le K A^{-n}b_n,\quad A^n\widetilde r_n/b_n=\sum_{\omega\in E}\kappa_\omega\omega^n+O(n^{-1}),\quad\widetilde r_1=\rho
scope_limits: Here A is any positive constant, E is a fixed finite set of distinct unit complex phases, and the input majorant is assumed.
The error in C̃_n is absolute O_U(|u|A^(−n)b_n/n), with a removable quotient at u=0; positivity is unnecessary.
The expansion is additive when phases cancel. No general Borel continuation theorem follows from these coefficient hypotheses alone.
results.attribution_note: Explicit finite-phase synthesis of the same endpoint proof; not a priority claim for factorial asymptotic calculus.

results.label: cor:prefix
results.title: Polynomial changes of the forward tail

article_section.label: sec:phases
article_section.title: Finite phases and changes of the initial coefficients

results.claim_summary: For R+P with a fixed polynomial P(0)=0, only p_1=[t]P changes the leading two action amplitudes.
scope_limits: The leading amplitudes are unchanged when P(t)=O(t²); the weaker condition deg P≥2 is insufficient.
Does not assert that arbitrary perturbations preserve the original odd valuation or the first-correction formula.
results.attribution_note: A direct specialization of the finite-phase theorem.

results.label: lem:second-endpoint
results.title: The second endpoint contribution
results.claim_summary: Uniformly isolates the first two endpoint configurations, including one additional forward index of size two, with a remainder strong enough for the first inverse-index correction.
scope_limits: n≥12 and 1≤k≤n/2; the second term is zero for k=1.
B_* and the implied constant are independent of n,k. The complementary k range is controlled separately by the factorial majorant.
results.attribution_note: Direct Gamma-convolution estimate supporting the first correction.

results.label: cor:relative-two-term
results.title: Relative uniformity down to the resonant endpoint
results.claim_summary: The two-term asymptotic expansion is relative and uniform down to u=0 on every bounded positive interval; the correction ratios have finite endpoint limits.
scope_limits: Real 0<u≤U; no lower bound on u.
No general complex relative statement is claimed at zeros of H_ε(cu).
results.attribution_note: Uses the improved odd remainder, not division of an unqualified absolute error by a vanishing amplitude.

results.label: thm:Borel-models
results.title: Boundary models with controlled remainders

article_section.label: sec:Borel
article_section.title: Logarithmic and dilogarithmic Borel boundary models

results.claim_summary: The Borel transform admits explicit logarithmic and logarithmic–dilogarithmic models with C⁰ and C¹ closed-disk remainders respectively; both ±A are genuine singularities for every complex u≠0 and the exact radius is A.
scope_limits: The remainders are holomorphic in |ξ|<A; H₀ extends continuously to the closed disk, and H₁ and its complex derivative do so. All extensions are locally uniform in u.
At u=0 the transform is identically zero. For u≠0 the radial logarithmic coefficients (2u/A)e^(−cu) and −(2u/A)e^(cu) do not vanish.
Boundary regularity does not identify a complete local singular germ or imply holomorphic extension through ±A.
results.attribution_note: Direct consequence of coefficient estimates, independent of the subsequent continuation theorem; strengthens the predecessor’s fixed-positive-u radius result.

results.label: prop:forward-Borel
results.title: A normally convergent logarithmic lattice
results.claim_summary: The full forward tail has the stated logarithmic divisor-lattice Borel transform, with normal continuation on compact subsets of the path surface avoiding Aℤ.
scope_limits: The principal expression is holomorphic off the real cuts (−∞,−A] and [A,∞), with a removable value at zero.
The large-m tail is controlled by Σd(m)/m²; only finitely many terms acquire monodromy along a fixed bounded path.
Zero may acquire a pole on another sheet. The formula includes the linear coefficient −1/4 in Borel space.
results.attribution_note: The explicit forward kernel is inherited; the path-continuation proof and full-tail convention are supplied directly here.

results.label: prop:Sauzin-input
results.title: Nonlinear resurgence and summability closure
results.claim_summary: For a closed discrete additive set Ω containing zero, Ω-resurgent series are closed under convergent analytic substitution; maps x+R_Ω form a composition/inversion group. The corresponding operations preserve 1-summability in an arc and commute with summation on smaller common sectors.
scope_limits: Analytic substitutions require zero-constant inputs. The infinity-coordinate maps are tangent to the identity, G(x)=x+O(1).
The continuation and summability assertions include their respective analytic control hypotheses; formal existence alone is insufficient.
No new proof of the quoted convolution estimates is claimed.
results.attribution_note: Sauzin2015, Theorems 3 and 5 and summable counterparts 3′ and 5′, used with Ω=Aℤ.

results.label: thm:inverse-continuation
results.title: Continuation of the quadratic inverse
results.claim_summary: For every fixed complex u, the shifted Borel germ of V continues along every path starting at zero and thereafter avoiding Aℤ.
scope_limits: Fixed u; the case u=0 is trivial. Multiplication by x is checked through differentiation of the Borel transform.
The theorem gives an allowed set, not the exact active lattice on each sheet.
No global simple-resurgence statement, complete local minor, or all-order alien derivative is proved.
results.attribution_note: A proved coordinate reduction followed by the established nonlinear closure theorem.

results.label: lem:kernel-growth
results.title: Growth of the forward kernel on nonreal rays
results.claim_summary: The principal forward Borel kernel has a uniform logarithmic-square bound on closed angular regions separated from both real directions.
scope_limits: 0<δ<π/2; δ≤arg ξ≤π−δ or −π+δ≤arg ξ≤−δ.
This is a principal-branch angular bound, not a bound on arbitrary continuation sheets.
results.attribution_note: Elementary divisor summation and head–tail estimate, proved to verify the hypotheses needed for summability.

results.label: thm:inverse-summability
results.title: Sectorial sums satisfy the inverse equation
results.claim_summary: For fixed complex u, V is 1-summable in every direction θ∉πℤ; its sum is the unique O(q) solution of the exact summed implicit equation on sufficiently small common sectors.
scope_limits: Fixed u; summation and inversion are compared on smaller common sectors.
Uses growth control in addition to continuation, with Cauchy estimates for the differentiation step.
No ordinary convergence of the factorial q-series, uniformity over unbounded u, or identification with an arithmetic inverse average is asserted.
results.attribution_note: Application of summable nonlinear closure plus a local contraction proof of uniqueness.

results.label: prop:Stokes-transport
results.title: Leading inverse jump with its shifted amplitude

article_section.label: sec:Stokes
article_section.title: Compatibility with the exact Stokes transport

results.claim_summary: The exact forward lateral jump transports through the quadratic inverse with a uniform first-action law and an absolute second-exponential error; the finite amplitude shift exp(−Au/4) is retained.
scope_limits: Real q→0+, uniformly for real 0<u≤U; the admissible upper bound on q may depend on U.
V_± are defined using the exact lateral completions R_ex±J/2 and the upper-minus-lower sign convention.
The result is not an all-order local Borel or alien-calculus statement, and does not identify arithmetic averaging after inversion with nonlinear median summation.
results.attribution_note: The exact forward completion and inverse transport principle are predecessor results. The present contribution is the proved uniform leading estimate and its controlled amplitude shift.
